sorry_details.sorry_reason: Core step: showing that a holomorphic function with a critical point of order n ≥ 2 at a real point maps some non-real point near it to a real value. Requires Rouché's theorem, the argument principle, or a delicate IVT argument on Im(f(x₀ + r·e^{iα})) — none readily available in Mathlib.
proved_lemmas: order_ge_two_of_deriv_zero: order of f - f(x₀) at x₀ is ≥ 2 when f'(x₀) = 0
exists_factorization_of_order_ge_two: local factorization f(z)-f(x₀) = (z-x₀)^n · g(z) with g(x₀) ≠ 0
deriv_ne_zero_on_reals: main theorem (modulo the sorry boundary)

proof_notes.strategy: Proof by contradiction. Assume f'(x₀)=0 for real x₀. Then f-f(x₀) has order n≥2 at x₀, giving local factorization (z-x₀)^n · g(z) with g(x₀)≠0. The n-to-1 local structure produces non-real preimages of real values, contradicting f(z)∈ℝ ⟹ z∈ℝ.
